spec.title: Quicklens and shared ZAP client workflows

status.comment: Owner-authorized layer above the headless communication foundation; this document does not claim a completed graphical client.

p.shared-client: Quicklens is the practical browser and Electron client within org.vibevm.zap/lens. Qwik 2 owns the reusable renderer, Sigma.js renders a Graphology MultiDirectedGraph, and a shared client model owns decoded semantic objects, selection, questions and plan operations. Gamelens may later replace the presentation while reusing those contracts. Codlens includes the planned VS Code and IntelliJ IDEA integrations and agent-facing integration assets. PROP-005 defines the shared application server, multi-project workspaces, managed coordinators, chat, rich questions and history used by all Lens clients. Browser code imports only explicit platform-safe seams; the broker, filesystem, credentials and Electron main process remain outside the renderer dependency graph.

p.read-model: A configured ZAP service supplies its actual capabilities and exact active planning context. The client discovers the active outcome, current strategy and adopted milestone plan through registered bounded queries. It never guesses those identities from an event tail or requires a human to paste them. Missing state, stale indexes, incomplete pages and unavailable capabilities have explicit views. Snapshot, query and continuation identities remain consistent; mismatched revisions cause refresh rather than mixing records from different plans. Unsigned integer values retain their exact wire meaning without JavaScript precision loss.

p.semantic-map: The graph preserves typed object references and parallel directed relationships. Selecting a task, milestone, resource or other object opens a structured card with its available name, purpose, status, relationships, acceptance meaning and provenance. Optional difficulty, complexity, effort, waiting and uncertainty remain separate; missing measurements are visibly unknown. Visual positions, colors and symbols are client presentation and never become planning facts. Graph search, type/status filters and navigation remain usable with partial or empty data. A demonstration dataset is explicitly labelled and never presented as the user's live plan.

p.plan-control: Agent tools, ordinary agent chat and Quicklens controls address the same ZAP plan authority. Human intent can request a new or revised plan while existing work runs. The client supports plan reads, proposals, current-state previews, applicable decisions, admitted operations, status and reconciliation through the service's registered public interfaces. The trusted adapter preserves ZAP economics, holds and authority. An operation uses the exact store, base, revision and command identity; an uncertain response is reconciled before retry. Unsupported operations are disabled with a useful reason. Existing scoped Owner authorization is respected and does not acquire a redundant GUI confirmation requirement.

p.specification-drift: A background specification change signal is advisory. Before preparing or admitting a revision, the integration verifies the relevant captured source basis. Added or changed specifications become reassessment input and cannot grant new authority by their contents. The successor preview identifies affected work; affected running results retain their prior source and plan basis until reconciled. Unaffected work may continue. Changed plans or source captures invalidate stale previews. The ordinary agent text flow remains available during this process.

p.interaction: Questions and answers use the shared durable broker. The UI shows their addressed actor, pending/answered/cancelled/expired state and explicit amendment history where available. Answering one actor's question cannot satisfy another actor's request or approve an unrelated plan change. Disconnect and restart preserve actionable state and expose reconnect/resynchronization. Rendering and user waits never hold an agent tool call open.

p.shells: One built Qwik renderer serves browser and Electron shells. Light and dark themes are explicit, persist the user's preference, and apply to both the graph and cards. Electron uses context isolation and sandboxing with Node integration disabled in the renderer; a narrow bridge exposes only necessary application operations. Local HTTP access retains the broker's origin and role checks. Source maps and implementation errors are not the ordinary product flow; readable recovery actions are.

p.acceptance: Acceptance exercises a real configured ZAP query and at least one admitted plan-change/reconciliation path, simultaneous agent questions, stale plan/source rejection, structured cards, graph selection/search/filter, both themes, and the same renderer in browser and Electron. TypeScript discipline and production builds pass. Browser imports cannot resolve privileged modules. Visual inspection verifies usable layout, readable cards and empty/error states. Synthetic fixtures, live host inference and real backend execution are reported as different evidence.
